info.text:
In 2025 the US imported $308.7 billion of goods from China, about $2,290 per household, even after a drop of almost a third. We follow the money: what Americans buy, who really pays a tariff (with lamp math), why China buys half of US soybean exports, why China's $618 billion of Treasuries matters, and what China's slowdown and factory prices mean for prices here.

0:00 Intro
0:42 The stuff in your cart
2:20 Who pays the tariff
4:04 China the customer
5:25 China the lender
6:47 When China slows down
8:23 The recap

Sources:
- US Census Bureau, trade in goods with China (2018-2025)

- China National Bureau of Statistics: 2025 GDP; CPI and PPI for August 2026
- China customs 2025 trade data via NBC News (Jan 2026)
- CNN (Sept 28, 2026) and Time (Sept 29, 2026) on the US-China tariff cuts
- Amiti, Redding and Weinstein, Journal of Economic Perspectives (2019)
- Federal Reserve FEDS Notes (Aug 2, 2024)
- USDA Foreign Agricultural Service (2024); farmdoc daily (Sept 2025)
- Fortune and NBC News (2025) on the de minimis rule

News and education, not financial advice.
